children: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen touted plans to further speed up permitting and safeguard the access to critical raw materials as officials seek to boost the bloc's competitiveness.

"In today's economy, speed is of the essence," the European Union chief said on Wednesday during a speech in Strasbourg that touched on a broad range of subjects from agriculture and climate to relations with China.
She said permits and financing can determine where investments are made and that the bloc needs to move much faster.

She also said the EU needs a pact against gold-plating--where governments add extra restrictions or provisions on top of existing rules--if officials are serious about simplifying the region's regulations.
